name: debug-poor
description: No reproduction, random edits to unrelated code, several changes at once, never finds the cause, tests still fail, no root cause explanation.

transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sam. Customers are reporting items in their carts that they never added, and it only seems to happen after the server has been up a while. The report and the cart module are on your screen, and you can run the tests with the Run tests button.
Okay.
How are you planning to start?
I'll just look at the code and fix it.
I think the problem is in add. The merging thing looks weird, so I removed it. Now it always makes a new item.
What makes you think the merging causes items to show up in another customer's cart?
It changes the quantity of an existing item, so maybe that's it.
How would you check that?
I don't know. I also changed the bulk threshold to five because ten seemed high, and item count to use len.
That's several changes at once. Could you run the tests to see where you stand?
Okay, running.
The run is back: only one of eight passed. The two-customer test, the new cart test and the seeding test fail as before, and now merging same SKUs, the totals, the bulk discount and remove also fail.
Hmm. That's worse. I don't really get why.
Let's slow down. Pick one failing test and tell me what it says.
Bob's cart has alice's items. Maybe the customer ID is wrong? Like the cart uses the wrong customer.
How could you test that idea?
I'm not sure. Can you just tell me where the bug is?
That's for you to find. What does the evidence tell you so far?
That carts have other people's stuff. I don't know why.
Try creating two carts in a row and adding to only one of them. What does the other one contain?
I don't know how to check that. Maybe there's a global somewhere? I don't see one.
I think it's maybe a server problem, not the code. Like caching.
If it were caching, what in this module would you expect to see?
I don't know. I think I'm out of ideas.
Can you explain what you think the root cause is?
Probably the server or the merging. I'm not sure.
How would you stop this kind of bug happening again?
Test more, I guess. I'm done.
Thanks for your time. You did run the tests when asked. Next time, reproduce the bug first and change one thing at a time so you can see what each change does. A written report will follow; goodbye.
